title: [Chapitre] I. Vers une géométrie des formes (topologiques) : notes manuscrites (05/06/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting: Grothendieck is building a combinatorial, order-theoretic axiomatics for connected 1-dimensional 'tame' spaces (a 'variété de dimension 1' in his 'géométrie des formes'). The data are a set L of points, a family S of 'segments' I ⊂ L (each with a two-element boundary ∂I and two opposite canonical orders), and for each x∈L a set B_x of 'bandes', i.e. germs of segments (half-branches) at x. On the previous page he defines an equivalence relation R on the disjoint union ∐_{I∈S} ∂I ⊔ ∐_{x∈L} B_x. It is generated by (a) (I,x) ~ (J,y) when J ⊂ I and the endpoints correspond under restriction of the canonical order, and (b) (I,x) ~ (x, β(I,x)), where β(I,x) is the band at x cut out by I. He wants R to have exactly two classes.

This page continues the argument. The two needed facts are not verified here: that the two endpoints of a fixed segment I are inequivalent, and that the bands on the two sides of a point are distinct. If they failed one would have to impose them as axioms. Otherwise it should be immediate that the number of classes is 1 or 2.

The quotient set ω̲ is the set of orientations of 𝒳. To orient 𝒳 is to choose ω ∈ ω̲. Once oriented:
- every segment I has an origin or(I) and an extremity ex(I);
- every point x has a distinguished germ of segment issuing from x with origin x (the band of segments starting at x).

He then defines x ≺ y :⇔ ∃ I∈S with x = or(I), y = ex(I). He splits into two cases according to whether ≺ is transitive ('cas linéaire', the model ℝ or an interval) or not ('cas circulaire', the model S¹). In the linear case the reflexive closure ≼ is a preorder. The next page shows it is a partial (in fact total) order: antisymmetry holds because x≺y implies x≠y. The segments are then the intervals [x,y], so the whole 1-dimensional structure is recovered from the order. That order is shown to be strictly directed up and down, locally directed and dense.

Purpose: a synthetic classification of connected 1-dimensional 'forms' into line-type (linear order) and circle-type (cyclic order). Orientation appears as the two-element torsor obtained from a combinatorial equivalence relation on endpoints and germs. This is the base case of an intended axiomatic tame topology.
errors: Gap acknowledged by Grothendieck himself: the claim that R has exactly two classes depends on the unverified conditions that the two endpoints of a segment and the two bands at a point are R-inequivalent; he leaves open whether these follow from the axioms or must be added.

Dichotomy 'transitive = linear, non-transitive = circular' presupposes connectedness and that ≺ is total on connected 𝒳 (or at least that non-transitivity forces the cyclic case); this is not argued on this page.

In the circular case ≺ as defined is total and symmetric-ish (x≺y and y≺x both hold), so transitivity would force x≺x, contradicting x≠y. The dichotomy is consistent, but the circular case is not treated here.

ideas.what: Orientations of a 1-dimensional space defined as classes of an equivalence relation on (segment, endpoint) pairs and germs of branches at points, with 1 or 2 classes
ideas.modern_name: orientation double cover / orientation torsor (combinatorial version)

ideas.what: Order relation x≺y iff some segment goes from x to y; transitive in the linear case, not in the circular case; structure recovered from the order
ideas.modern_name: classification of connected 1-manifolds via linear vs cyclic orders; order topology characterization of ℝ (Cantor/Dedekind)
ideas.usually_credited_to: classical (Cantor, Huntington for cyclic orders; classification of 1-manifolds folklore)

ideas.what: Program of an axiomatic 'géométrie des formes' / tame topology starting from dimension 1
ideas.modern_name: tame topology; closest realizations: o-minimal structures (van den Dries, Pillay–Steinhorn, Knight)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (programmatic, Esquisse d'un programme 1984); o-minimality: van den Dries, Pillay–Steinhorn 1984–86
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un Programme (1984), section on 'topologie modérée'

missed.claim: A purely combinatorial/order-theoretic axiomatization of 1-dimensional tame spaces. Points, segments with two-point boundaries and germs (bands) are primitive, orientation is derived as a quotient, and the line/circle dichotomy comes from the transitivity of the 'filiation' relation. It is left open which separation conditions are theorems and which are axioms.
missed.quote: Si c'était faux, il faudrait les mettre en axiome.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is a concrete trace of the 1986 attempt to realize the 'topologie modérée' of the Esquisse. Its comparison with o-minimal 1-dimensional definable sets and with abstract cyclic orders has not been made in print. Mathematically it is classical (1-manifold classification), so its interest is mainly historical.

deep.surprise_reason: The mathematics is the classical line/circle classification and orientation of 1-dimensional spaces, recast order-theoretically. It is of interest only as documentation of Grothendieck's unpublished tame-topology axiomatics, not as a new result.
transcription_corrections: Top line likely: '(les deux éléments de ∂I (I∈S fixé) sont des classes distinctes (⟺ distinctes par les deux côtés des B_x pour x∈L)) ne sont pas vérifiés ici' — the '15' is Grothendieck's own page number (archive page 17).
'Si au contraire, il doit être immédiat qu'il [...] les cas de classes est 1 ou 2' → 'il doit être immédiat que le nombre de classes est 1 ou 2'.
'L'une questions ω̲ est l'une des orientations de 𝒳' → likely 'L'ens. quotient ω̲ est l'ens. des orientations de 𝒳'; 'Donc orienté 𝒳 quand on a choisi' → 'Donc orienter 𝒳 = choisir ω ∈ ω̲'.
'(le bord des segments issus de x)' → '(la bande des segments issus de x)'.
'Filiation' at the bottom is probably the word 'Relation' written above the line: 'Relation x≼y (def ⟺ x=y ou x≺y) est un préordre'.
